claims.text: Local mechanical-stress and temperature peaks during elevated-temperature wear disrupt the protective oxide film on the eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Oxide-film breakdown exposes the reactive alloy substrate to the corrosive environment.
Corrosion of the exposed substrate further accelerates wear, creating a positive feedback cycle.
The material is a multiphase eutectic AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 high-entropy alloy fabricated by powder metallurgy.
The alloy initially has a conformal transient oxide film formed under high-temperature ambient conditions.
The initial oxide film protects the underlying alloy from corrosion.
Oxide-film integrity is lost when local stress and temperature exceed a critical threshold.
Frictional heating and localized mechanical contact generate repetitive stress spikes that fracture the oxide film.
Film disruption intensifies corrosion of the exposed alloy.
Enhanced corrosion creates pits that further weaken the remaining oxide film.
The wear-corrosion feedback produces a nonlinear threshold increase in total degradation.
Above the critical stress-temperature limit, corrosion current density increases sharply.
Above the critical stress-temperature limit, wear volume increases sharply.
Below the threshold, the intact oxide film maintains relatively moderate degradation.
A baseline that preserves oxide-film integrity will have lower wear volume than the oxide-breakdown condition.
A baseline that preserves oxide-film integrity will have lower corrosion current than the oxide-breakdown condition.
The proposed mechanism is applicable between 600 and 700 degrees Celsius.
The mechanism requires oxygen partial pressures that permit formation of a transient protective oxide.
Varying mechanical load and oxygen partial pressure while measuring oxide integrity, corrosion current, wear volume, temperature, and modeled stress provides the proposed controlled comparison.
Failure to observe a sharp corrosion-current and wear-volume jump correlated with local stress-temperature peaks and oxide breakdown would falsify the proposed mechanism.
